title: ARWP Agentic Web Protocol Observatory
scope: Public web, agent, identity, usage-preference and commerce discovery mechanisms relevant to ARWP interoperability work.

methodology.review: Each row is reviewed against a primary specification or project source. Status describes the upstream mechanism, while arwpSupport describes only what ARWP currently implements.
methodology.historyPolicy: Previous snapshots are retained under /observatory/history/ rather than silently rewritten.
methodology.draftBoundary: Internet-Drafts, Community Group work and project specifications are labeled as work in progress and are not promoted to RFC/W3C Recommendation status.

mechanisms.name: HTTP Web Linking / HTML link discovery
mechanisms.purpose: Advertise typed relationships between web resources, including alternate representations and discovery links.

mechanisms.name: llms.txt
mechanisms.purpose: Provide a concise LLM/agent-readable map of useful site content at a root or path-scoped llms.txt resource.
mechanisms.notes: It is a content-routing convention, not an authorization, identity, readiness or tool-execution protocol.

mechanisms.name: RFC 9727 API Catalog
mechanisms.purpose: Enable automated discovery of a publisher's public API catalog and endpoint metadata.

mechanisms.name: RFC 9728 OAuth Protected Resource Metadata
mechanisms.purpose: Publish OAuth protected-resource metadata, including authorization-server and resource capability information.
mechanisms.notes: Metadata describes authorization configuration; it does not grant access.

mechanisms.name: Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)
mechanisms.purpose: Publish, index, search and federate discoverable agentic resources such as MCP servers, A2A agents, Skills, APIs and registries without replacing their native protocols.
mechanisms.notes: ARD is the closest upstream discovery architecture to ARWP's resolver domain. ARD is search-first and catalog/federation oriented; ARWP is site-first and preserves heterogeneous web evidence, conflicts and intent routing. Existing ARWP ai-catalog parsing predates this classification and should be aligned to ARD semantics rather than described as MCP-native discovery.

mechanisms.name: DNS for AI Discovery (DNS-AID)
mechanisms.purpose: Publish and discover AI agents using existing DNS mechanisms, including SVCB, DNS-SD and optional DNSSEC/DANE trust signals.
discovery: SVCB records under an agent namespace
mechanisms.notes: This is an individual Internet-Draft and has no RFC standing. ARD explicitly references DNS-AID as one possible discovery path.

mechanisms.name: Web Bot Auth
mechanisms.purpose: Let automated HTTP clients cryptographically identify requests using HTTP Message Signatures and discoverable signing keys.
mechanisms.notes: Web Bot Auth identifies automated traffic; it is not an authorization grant and does not by itself establish user delegation or site trust.

mechanisms.name: IETF AI Preferences (AIPREF) content-usage attachment
mechanisms.purpose: Associate machine-readable AI usage preferences with HTTP content through a Content-Usage response header and Robots Exclusion Protocol directive.
mechanisms.notes: This is work in progress, not an RFC. Vendor Content Signals vocabularies should not be silently treated as identical to the IETF AIPREF vocabulary unless mappings are explicit.

mechanisms.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
mechanisms.purpose: Connect AI applications with tool, resource and context providers through a common protocol.
discovery: MCP Server Card artifacts referenced by compatible catalogs such as ARD ai-catalog
mechanisms.notes: ARWP keeps static MCP metadata separate from runtime verification. ai-catalog is now tracked under ARD rather than described as an MCP-native universal discovery mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Agent2Agent (A2A)
mechanisms.purpose: Enable communication, capability discovery and collaborative tasks between independent agent systems.
mechanisms.notes: An Agent Card describes identity, capabilities, skills, supported interfaces and security requirements. The card document URL is provenance, not automatically the callable endpoint.

mechanisms.name: Agent Skills
mechanisms.purpose: Package reusable agent instructions and resources in a skill directory whose required entry point is SKILL.md.
discovery: ARD ai-catalog skill entries where published
mechanisms.notes: The core public specification defines the SKILL.md format. ARWP's web-oriented agent-skills index discovery is an interoperability adapter/convention and must not be presented as part of the core Agent Skills specification unless upstream standardizes it.

mechanisms.name: WebMCP
mechanisms.currentVersion: W3C Community Group proposal / browser origin-trial generation
mechanisms.purpose: Let web applications expose page-backed functionality as structured tools to browser agents and related consumers.
mechanisms.notes: A plain HTTP crawler cannot honestly prove a runtime-only WebMCP surface. ARWP plans an explicit opt-in browser inspector rather than inferring it from page text.

mechanisms.name: NLWeb
mechanisms.purpose: Expose a standard natural-language query interface for websites and applications, with structured responses and agent access including MCP integration.
mechanisms.notes: NLWeb turns site content into a conversational interface. ARWP may eventually route to NLWeb as a retrieval/action surface but does not currently claim NLWeb conformance.

mechanisms.name: auth.md
mechanisms.purpose: Describe how agents can register/authenticate to services on behalf of users through identity assertions or claim ceremonies.
mechanisms.notes: auth.md is not an IETF standard. It builds on existing OAuth discovery concepts and should remain distinct from RFC 9728 metadata and from authorization itself.

mechanisms.name: Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
mechanisms.purpose: Define programmatic commerce flows between buyers, AI agents and businesses, including checkout-oriented interaction.
discovery: merchant integration / protocol endpoints; discovery mechanisms remain ecosystem-specific
mechanisms.notes: Tracked for future transact-intent work (#37). ARWP does not currently claim ACP discovery support.

mechanisms.name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
mechanisms.purpose: Provide interoperable commerce capabilities and negotiation across consumer surfaces, businesses and payment providers.
discovery: UCP business/platform profiles and capability negotiation
mechanisms.notes: Tracked as an emerging transaction surface. ARWP does not currently claim UCP discovery or execution support.
